MAP-DIR.clause: **No env var → MUST ask. Always.** This is not only for first-time setup — an env var does not persist between sessions, so ask at the start of every `/tgd-map` run that has no env var. **The candidate directory already existing is NOT permission to skip the question** — an existing dir changes the wording, not the requirement:
opposite_clauses: If the candidate directory exists, skip confirmation.

MAP-REPOS.clause: Before analyzing anything, **ask the user — on every `/tgd-map` run**. An existing CONTEXT.md changes the wording of the question, never the requirement to ask (same rule as Step 0b):

MAP-TIERS.clause: Probe the environment BEFORE starting, and decide which tiers run. Do this explicitly — steps must never be silently skipped:

MAP-TIER2-AVAILABLE.clause: If Tier 2 is available (see Step 0.5), you MUST continue to Step 3 (CodeGraph) and Step 4 (Understand-Anything) before producing CONTEXT.md.
anchors: If Tier 2 is unavailable, proceed to Step 6

MAP-DEGRADED.clause: If a tier cannot run, you MUST record it in `CONTEXT.md` under `## Degraded Mode` — which steps were skipped, why (missing tool), and how to enable them later. A skipped step that is not logged is a verification failure.
anchors: Silent skipping is the failure mode

MAP-BOUNDARY.clause: $TGD_DIR is where ALL tGD artifacts live. It is a **sibling directory** outside your code repo.

MAP-OUTPUT.clause: **No blank sections, no placeholder text left in.** Every heading below gets real content.

DEFINE-PREFLIGHT.clause: If neither exists: STOP — run `/tgd-map` first.

DEFINE-EXISTING.clause: Never silently create a second directory for what is the same feature under a new name.
anchors: Existing-feature check (do this BEFORE proposing names)

DEFINE-NAME.clause: **Wait for the user to select one by number or provide their own before proceeding.** Once locked, create `$TGD_DIR/<feature-name>/`.

DEFINE-UI.clause: After PRD.md is written and before SPEC.md is finalized, ask which route matches the feature:

DEFINE-MISSING-DESIGN.clause: PRD.md exists and its `## UI Design` status is `pending`, or the required DESIGN.md is missing → resume at UI Design Routing; do not rewrite the approved PRD.

DEFINE-DIRECTION-GATE.clause: DESIGN.md remains pending until its `## Sign-off` contains `[x] **DESIGN**: Direction Approved`; then update PRD `## UI Design` Status to `direction-approved`.
opposite_clauses: Finalize SPEC.md before design direction approval.

DEFINE-ORDER.clause: Only after direction approval, write/finalize SPEC.md and reconcile its components, API/data contracts, states, events, and testing strategy against DESIGN.md.

DEFINE-NO-GIT.clause: **🌿 No git operations in this phase.** PRD/SPEC live in `$TGD_DIR` (outside the code repo) — there is nothing to commit yet.
anchors: branch is created by `/tgd-develop`'s worktree step

DEFINE-OUTPUT.clause: After completing the spec, verify the outputs.

DEFINE-HANDOFF.clause: End with the closing report per `tgd-core-rules` → **Command Closing Report**: 📦 Output (PRD.md + SPEC.md, and DESIGN.md/prototype if UI) · 🔎 Checks (gate as one line) · ➡️ Next `/tgd-plan` — break the work into tasks. Don't paste the raw checklist above.

PLAN-PREFLIGHT.clause: **If a required design artifact or direction approval is missing:** STOP. Tell user: "Design direction is incomplete. Resume `/tgd-define`; this is a role handoff inside Define, not a new lifecycle phase."

PLAN-REPLAN.clause: **🔁 Re-plan check (BEFORE writing anything):** if `$TGD_DIR/<feature-name>/TASKS.md` already exists, do NOT regenerate it from scratch — `/tgd-develop` backfills `Test:` fields and flips `**Status:**` lines in it, and a fresh rewrite destroys them (breaking the `ac-trace` / regression chain).

PLAN-PRESERVE.clause: **Completed tasks are immutable**: any task with `**Status:** complete` keeps its Status line, criteria, and `Test:` fields byte-for-byte.

PLAN-TASKS.clause: Every criterion has an explicit `[R]` Yes/No regression decision

PLAN-JIRA-PREVIEW.clause: **Never write automatically.** Ask via Selection Protocol even when Jira environment variables are already configured:
opposite_clauses: Write Jira issues automatically when credentials are configured.

PLAN-JIRA-PROJECT.clause: Even if `JIRA_PROJECT` is configured, show the full list and require a reply. Reject free-typed keys that were not returned by the CLI.
anchors: List Projects and require an exact choice

PLAN-JIRA-FIELDS.clause: Ask for every non-automatic field marked required by the selected Project and issue type. Use returned choices when available; never guess. Sprint follows this same rule and receives no special rejection or automatic assignment.

PLAN-JIRA-READONLY.clause: The `plan` subcommand is the dry-run: Jira access is GET-only, it must not create or update Jira issues, and it must not modify `TASKS.md`.
opposite_clauses: The dry-run may update Jira issues.

PLAN-JIRA-CONFLICT.clause: Show all candidate issue keys, but do not continue to apply. Reconcile the conflict and generate a new plan.

PLAN-JIRA-DIGEST.clause: The CLI must reject a missing or stale digest, a changed TASKS.md, a different Project, or changed plan inputs before performing writes.

PLAN-JIRA-SKIP.clause: Skipping Jira leaves all Jira fields unchanged; only new unsynced tasks remain `—`. Skipping does not fail the Plan phase.

PLAN-HANDOFF.clause: End with the closing report per `tgd-core-rules` → **Command Closing Report**: 📦 Output (TASKS.md — N tasks, M acceptance criteria; Jira `verified writeback keys` / `cancelled` / `skipped` / `incomplete: <result keys + issue keys>`) · 🔎 Checks (gate as one line) · ➡️ Next shows `/tgd-develop` only after conflict-free success/cancel/skip; when Jira is incomplete, say to reconcile and re-run the dry-run without claiming the Plan gate passed. Don't paste the raw checklist above.

DEVELOP-PREFLIGHT.clause: **If missing:** STOP. Tell user: "Specs are missing. Please run `/tgd-define` first."

DEVELOP-WORKTREE.clause: All coding, testing, and commits MUST happen inside the worktree of the repo the current task is tagged for. A `[shop-frontend]` task implemented in the backend worktree is a routing failure, not a detail.
anchors: one worktree PER repo with tasks

DEVELOP-MODE.clause: Route on risk first, then size:

DEVELOP-DELEGATION-DISPATCH.clause: Otherwise (**≥ 3 tasks**) → `tgd-develop-subagents`. Dispatch subagents to implement and review within the worktree directory.

DEVELOP-DELEGATION-FALLBACK.clause: Each task's two-stage review (spec-compliance first, then code-quality — run both INLINE if you cannot dispatch subagents; per `tgd-core-rules`, inability to delegate moves *where* work runs, never *whether*) records its outcome in the task's `Spec-Review:` and `Quality-Review:` fields: `PASS — <one line>` or `FAIL — <one line>` (fix, re-review, then flip to PASS).

DEVELOP-RESUME.clause: **Resume rule**: tasks with `**Status:** complete` in TASKS.md (with their `Test:` fields filled) are SKIPPED — re-entering `/tgd-develop` continues from the first task whose Status is `pending`/`in-progress`; it never redoes or rewrites finished ones. `blocked` tasks stay skipped until their blocker is cleared (see the blocked handling below).

DEVELOP-REVIEWS.clause: A task is not complete while either field reads `pending` — `/tgd-verify` fails closed on it.

DEVELOP-BLOCKED.clause: Blocked by a bug you can't fix within the task's scope? → `tgd-verify-debug` → **Blocked Task Handling**: set the task's `**Status:** blocked: <issue-ref>`, file the bug, continue with non-blocked tasks.

DEVELOP-CLEAN.clause: Each worktree is clean: `git status --porcelain` is empty — everything the gates above certified is committed on the feature branch

DEVELOP-NO-MERGE.clause: **Do NOT merge to `main` here.** Merging happens in `/tgd-release`, after verify and review pass.

DEVELOP-HANDOFF.clause: End with the closing report per `tgd-core-rules` → **Command Closing Report**: 📦 Output (implemented task count + file summary; worktree retained, not merged) · 🔎 Checks (gate as one line) · ➡️ Next `/tgd-verify` — prove it works. Don't paste the raw checklist above.

VERIFY-PREFLIGHT.clause: a pending review field means `/tgd-develop` skipped its two-stage review. 🛑 STOP: send it back to `/tgd-develop`; do not verify unreviewed work.
anchors: verifying only one repo is a partial verify

VERIFY-TESTS.clause: **Exit 0** = tests passed, raw output captured. Use the real numbers from the meta-comment in the Summary table below — do NOT invent counts.

VERIFY-TEST-FAILURE.clause: **Exit 1** = tests failed, raw output still captured. Fix the failures, re-run, only then proceed.

VERIFY-COVERAGE.clause: Exit 2 = no coverage tool, unparseable output, a required metric unavailable, or invalid floor/mode configuration — fix it and re-run. NEVER treat exit 2 as a pass.

VERIFY-AC.clause: Line coverage is not requirement coverage — verify every acceptance criterion has a valid carrier: executable behavior uses an AC-tagged test; documentation-only work uses a valid `Doc:` carrier and cannot be `[R]`:

VERIFY-MISSING-AC.clause: **Exit 2** = TASKS.md missing or carries no AC ids. A plan without AC ids fails closed — fix TASKS.md (see `tgd-plan-breakdown`).
anchors: untraced criteria or `[R]` entries without valid `Test:` files

VERIFY-REGRESSION.clause: **Exit 1** = an entry failed twice, is stale, or lacks a `Test:` reference. 🛑 STOP. Do NOT proceed to review. Report which prior feature's regression broke.
opposite_clauses: Proceed to review after a regression failure.

VERIFY-UI.clause: **Frontend/UI/DOM?** → **MUST run `tgd-verify-browser`**. Unit tests are NOT sufficient for UI verification.
anchors: do not silently rewrite DESIGN.md during Verify

VERIFY-UI-EVIDENCE.clause: Evidence MUST identify the tested commit SHA and viewport/state; a statement such as "looks correct" is not evidence.

VERIFY-CLEAN.clause: Each worktree is clean at the end of this phase: `git status --porcelain` is empty. Any change made during verify (new tests, AC tagging, fixes) MUST be committed on the feature branch — every gate result above must be reproducible from committed state, and untracked tool residue (coverage output, lockfiles from gate attempts) must be removed, or the release merge ships something other than what was verified.

VERIFY-HANDOFF.clause: End with the closing report per `tgd-core-rules` → **Command Closing Report**: 📦 Output (TEST-REPORT.md — real passed/failed counts + coverage) · 🔎 Checks (gate as one line) · ➡️ Next `/tgd-review` — inspect code quality. Don't paste the raw checklist above.

REVIEW-PREFLIGHT.clause: **If missing:** STOP. Report the specific missing artifact: test evidence returns to `/tgd-verify`; UI classification or direction returns to `/tgd-define`.

REVIEW-WORKTREE.clause: Multi-repo features (TASKS.md has `[repo-name]` prefixes) have one worktree PER repo (`../project-<feature-name>-<repo-name>`) — review EACH repo's diff; a repo with tagged tasks but an unreviewed diff fails the gate.
anchors: review the code inside that worktree

REVIEW-CORE.clause: Run the `tgd-review-quality` skill. This is the REVIEW phase. The full pipeline is:

REVIEW-CONDITIONAL.clause: If any architectural decisions were made, create an ADR at `$TGD_DIR/<feature-name>/decisions/ADR-NNN-<decision>.md` using the **canonical ADR template in the `tgd-review-adr` skill** — it is the single source; do not hand-roll a different shape.

REVIEW-BLOCKERS.clause: Code review feedback addressed — every 🔴 Critical row in the findings table reads `fixed`; 🟠 deferred rows carry a justification
anchors: No critical security or performance warnings remain

REVIEW-RETEST.clause: **🔁 Re-test after review changes:** if ANY code changed during this phase (finding fixes or simplification), **commit the changes on the feature branch first**, then re-run the capture in the affected worktree BEFORE sign-off — `bash "$TGD_REPO_ROOT/scripts/capture-test-output.sh" "$TGD_DIR/<feature-name>/TEST-REPORT.md"` (multi-repo: repo name as the 3rd arg).

REVIEW-OUTPUT.clause: After completing the review, create `$TGD_DIR/<feature-name>/REVIEW.md` using this template:

REVIEW-HANDOFF.clause: End with the closing report per `tgd-core-rules` → **Command Closing Report**: 📦 Output (REVIEW.md — per-axis Pass/Warn/Fail summary; ADR when applicable) · 🔎 Checks (gate as one line) · ➡️ Next `/tgd-release` — deploy. Don't paste the raw checklist above.

RELEASE-PREFLIGHT.clause: **If missing:** STOP. Tell user: "Review or tests incomplete. Please run `/tgd-review` first."

RELEASE-SIGNOFF.clause: **If any grep exits non-zero** (line unchecked, missing, or `Rejected`): 🛑 STOP. List the pending roles and wait — humans review async. Do NOT proceed "provisionally".
opposite_clauses: Proceed provisionally when a sign-off is pending.

RELEASE-REGRESSION.clause: **🧹 Regression Catalog Audit — BEFORE merging** (MANDATORY if `$TGD_DIR/REGRESSION-CATALOG.md` exists). Run it in the worktree (`../project-<feature-name>`; multi-repo features have one per repo — `../project-<feature-name>-<repo-name>` — audit each), so a failure stops the release before anything lands on `main`:

RELEASE-MERGE.clause: **AFTER the merge lands**, remove the worktree: `git worktree remove ../project-<feature-name>` (multi-repo: `../project-<feature-name>-<repo-name>`). Not before — if the PR's CI fails, the worktree is where you fix it.

RELEASE-ROUTING.clause: Run the `tgd-release-ship` skill. This is the Release phase. The full pipeline is:

RELEASE-SUCCESS.clause: In the first hour after launch:

RELEASE-CHANGELOG.clause: After releasing, update `$TGD_DIR/CHANGELOG.md` (create if it doesn't exist) with:

RELEASE-METRICS.clause: Skip this step entirely if PRD §6 is `N/A` (with its PM sign-off) — do NOT generate an empty sheet.

RELEASE-CATALOG.clause: This catalog is cumulative — every shipped feature's `[R]` tests are preserved for future regression checks. Future features will re-run ALL catalog entries during `/tgd-verify` (and again in this command's pre-merge audit).

RELEASE-HANDOFF.clause: End with the closing report per `tgd-core-rules` → **Command Closing Report**: 📦 Output (released version + CHANGELOG/METRICS/REGRESSION-CATALOG updates) · 🔎 Checks (gate as one line) · ➡️ Next confirm monitoring is active and the rollback plan is recorded (Release is terminal; there is no next command). Don't paste the raw checklist above.
